title: Derive exit codes and a freshness check from the ledger run outcome
description:
## What changes for the user
Today a daily run can finish with exit code 0 while a bank connection has been dead for a week or a walk was cut short. Once this lands, the process exit code says what happened (everything collected and fresh, something incomplete or stale, configuration missing, aborted), and a one-line summary on stderr names each incomplete walk and each stale connection.

## Outcome
Exit codes and a stderr summary are derived from the ledger's run and scope outcomes, and a freshness check per connection and per consent feeds the run outcome.

## Context
After cutover the default sync is the ledger path: a run closes `complete` when every `expected = 1` scope is `complete` or `unavailable` and no document is ambiguous, `partial` otherwise, `failed` on an exception, `interrupted` when a crash is swept on the next start. `unavailable` is a refusal the connector is known to make (the endpoint/status matrix: `/identity`, `/loans`, `/investments` on 404 or 403, first logical page only) and does not make a run partial.

Exit codes: `0` run `complete` and every item fresh; `1` run `partial`, or any item or consent stale (data was still saved); `2` configuration missing or invalid (as today); `3` run `failed` (authentication refused, unhandled exception). The recovery sweep's own result does not change the new run's exit code but is printed.

Freshness, per item: stale if `status != 'UPDATED'`, or `executionStatus != 'SUCCESS'`, or `lastUpdatedAt` older than 48 hours at run start (the provider syncs about every 24 hours; 48 tolerates one missed cycle). Per consent: stale if `expiresAt` is within 30 days or `revokedAt` is set. A stale item or consent sets the run `partial` and exit code 1, with the reason in the summary and in `runs.note`. Thresholds are named constants with the reason beside them.

Summary line on stderr: one line per incomplete or skipped `expected = 1` scope (`kind parent outcome error`) and one per stale item/consent, then the run outcome and exit code.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `pluggysync/freshness.py`, `pluggysync/run.py` (freshness hook at run close, summary), `pluggysync/cli.py` (exit codes), `README.md` (exit codes), `tests/test_exit_codes.py`, `tests/test_freshness.py`
**Reads only:** `pluggysync/ledger.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fixture run that closes `complete` with fresh items exits 0 and prints the outcome line only.
- [ ] A run with one `incomplete` expected scope exits 1 and the summary names that scope; a run with an `unavailable` `/identity` and nothing else wrong exits 0.
- [ ] An item with `lastUpdatedAt` 49 hours old, one with `status = 'LOGIN_ERROR'`, and a consent with `expiresAt` in 29 days each make the run `partial`, exit 1, and name the reason in the summary and in `runs.note`; 47 hours and 31 days do not.
- [ ] Missing `PLUGGY_CLIENT_ID` exits 2 before any write; an injected unhandled exception exits 3 with the run `failed`.
- [ ] Done when: `python3 -m unittest` passes with every case above.

## Tests
Unit over `pluggysync/freshness.py` (each threshold on both sides) and over the CLI exit path with a fake transport (each exit code).

title: Collect loans as an item-parented kind
description:
## What changes for the user
The bank connections already grant access to loan and credit-operation data (the consent includes `LOANS` and `CREDIT_OPERATIONS_ALL`, and two accounts pay overdraft interest every month), but nothing collects it. Once this lands, whatever the API publishes about loans for each connection is collected daily into the history like every other kind, and a connection that publishes none says so explicitly.

## Outcome
`loans` is one more item-parented kind in the ledger: planned per item, walked through `paged` on `/loans?itemId=`, archived, observed, projected into a `loans` table, covered by `--check` and `--reparse` like the other kinds. A 404 or 403 on the first logical page is `unavailable` per the existing matrix.

## Context
The consent of every connection lists `LOANS` and `CREDIT_OPERATIONS_ALL`, and two checking accounts in the data show `ENCARGOS_JUROS_CHEQUE_ESPECIAL` (overdraft interest) transactions, yet the collector never calls a loan endpoint. The endpoint's existence, path and page style must be confirmed against the Pluggy API reference before the first line of code, and which columns to extract is decided after reading one real response (projection columns beyond `id`, `item_id`, `raw`, `fetched_at` and the ledger columns are left open on purpose). The kind is already in the schema's `CHECK` lists (`scopes.kind`, `documents.kind`) and in the scope vocabulary, so no schema version bump is needed for the kind itself; a new projection table `loans` is a schema migration (version bump, guarded backup).

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `pluggysync/run.py` (plan and walk the kind), `pluggysync/projections.py` (`loans` table), `pluggysync/ledger.py` (migration adding the table), `pluggysync/views.py` (if a history view is warranted after seeing the data), `README.md`, `tests/test_loans.py`
**Reads only:** `pluggysync/walk.py`, `pluggysync/check.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Pluggy reference's loan endpoint path and page style are quoted in the PR before implementation.
- [ ] A fixture run with a recorded-shape loan page produces a `loans` scope per item, observations and projection rows; a 404 on the first page yields `unavailable` and the run stays `complete`; a 404 on page 2 yields `incomplete`.
- [ ] `--check` and `--reparse` handle the kind (a corrupted loan version body is reported; a reparse reproduces the rows).
- [ ] One real run shows, for each connection, either loan rows or an `unavailable` scope, recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Done when: `python3 -m unittest` passes and the real run is recorded.

## Tests
Unit over the kind's planning, walking and projection with a synthetic loan page; the real run is a manual acceptance step.

## Recovery path
The migration that adds `loans` is guarded by the `-pre-v<N>` backup; restoring it undoes the schema change.

title: Prove a failing run reaches the alert pipeline
description:
## What changes for the user
The alert for a failed run is assumed to work for this stack and has never been seen doing it. After this lands the operator has seen it arrive once, so a quiet phone means a good night rather than a broken alarm.

## Outcome
A deliberately failing Job against a copy of the ledger exits 3, `KubeJobFailed` fires for it, and the alert clears when the Job is deleted.

## Context
The chart's `KubeJobFailed` (`kube_job_failed > 0`, 15 minutes, severity warning) routes to ntfy. It is known to fire for another stack, so the pipeline is good; what this checks is that exit 3 from this image becomes a failed Job that reaches it. Refused credentials count as a failed run: no response archived and every walk refused.

The target is a copy, never the live file. A run appended to the ledger cannot be removed, and although an honest failed run is harmless, it is not worth putting in the permanent record for a test. Wrong credentials need no secret to be read: `check-job.yaml` carries no `envFrom`, so the Secret never enters this pod, and the Job sets all three variables to dummy values. The one API call is an `/auth` POST that the provider refuses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/srv/homelab/pluggy-sync/restore-test/pluggy.db` is a copy of `pluggy-snapshot.db`, mode 0600.
- [ ] A one-off Job from `check-job.yaml`, with `args` removed and `PLUGGY_DB=/data/restore-test/pluggy.db`, `PLUGGY_CLIENT_ID=wrong`, `PLUGGY_CLIENT_SECRET=wrong`, `PLUGGY_ITEM_IDS=wrong` set, ends `Failed` with exit code 3.
- [ ] The live `pluggy.db` has the same `max(runs.id)` before and after.
- [ ] Prometheus shows `KubeJobFailed` firing for that Job within 20 minutes, and the operator confirms the phone notification arrived.
- [ ] Deleting the Job clears the alert within 10 minutes.
- [ ] `restore-test/` is removed, so the next backup does not carry it.
- [ ] Done when: the above hold; the operator's confirmation is quoted in the close reason.

## Tests
- E2E: a real failing Job through the real alert pipeline to the real phone.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none in any repository. A temporary directory under `/srv/homelab/pluggy-sync/`, and a one-off Job not tracked by Argo.
**Reads only:** `apps/pluggy-sync/check-job.yaml`

The live ledger is not touched.

title: Import the two frozen legacy states into a candidate ledger
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the history collected since September 2026 exists as two frozen copies of the old database and would be lost to the new history-keeping database. Once this lands, both frozen states are imported as the first two observed days of the new database, so the balance of every caixinha on 2026-09-12 and on 2026-11-07 is queryable alongside everything collected afterwards.

## Outcome
`--candidate <path> --from-states <sep> <nov>` builds a candidate ledger database from the two frozen legacy copies, with every legacy row as an observation in the run whose time window contains its `fetched_at`, the legacy control tables preserved verbatim, projections rebuilt, and a manifest verification that fails the import on any mismatch. The live database is never opened.

## Context
The legacy database has nine resource tables written by upsert (latest copy only, `raw` = `json.dumps` of the parsed row, `fetched_at` per row), `sync_runs` (one row per run) and `probes` (one row per probed walk; consents and investment transactions were never probed; four kinds carry a hardcoded status 200). Two frozen copies exist beside `pluggy.db`, gitignored by `pluggy.db-*`: `pluggy.db-2026-09-12-state` (after run 2; 1,701 resource rows; runs 1–2) and `pluggy.db-2026-11-07-state` (after run 3; 2,019 resource rows; runs 1–3; 87 probe rows with 34 distinct `fetched_at`). Run 1 was truncated by a pagination bug and overwritten by run 2 a minute later, so no run-1 row survives. One row, a pending card purchase, appears in both copies with the same `fetched_at` in run 2: the collector never saw it again, and its posted twin has another id.

Rules:
- Inputs are explicit paths; no fallback to files beside the script, so a test on synthetic fixtures never reads real data. The import verifies that each state file's `sync_runs` and `probes` (order and all columns) are an exact prefix of the next's. Comparison against the **live** `pluggy.db` belongs to promotion, not here.
- `sync_runs` and `probes` are copied verbatim into `legacy_sync_runs` and `legacy_probes` (probe order as `seq`), never touched again.
- `sync_runs` rows become `runs` with `outcome = 'migrated'`, `code_version = 'unknown'`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `api_calls` copied, `note` copied with the import's remarks appended, `started_day`/`finished_day` computed, `item_ids` from that run's `/items/<id>` probe paths in order.
- Scopes: each `probes` row maps by path (`/categories` → `('categories','')`; `/items/<id>` → `items`; `/identity?itemId=` → `identities`; `/investments?itemId=` → `investments`; `/accounts?itemId=` → `accounts`; `/v2/transactions?accountId=` → `transactions`; `/bills?accountId=` → `bills`). Consents were attempted for every item whose `/items/<id>` probe is 200 (the legacy control flow), so a synthetic `consents` scope exists for each such `(run, item)` even with no surviving row; `investment_transactions` scopes for each `(run, investment)` where the investment was observed in that run or has movement observations; run 1's unknown coverage goes in `runs.note`. Every migrated scope: `expected = 1`, `outcome = 'incomplete'`, `infer_absence = 0`, `status` from `probes.status` (NULL for synthetic), `rows` = distinct documents migrated into it, `min_date`/`min_instant` NULL, `closed_at` = `probes.fetched_at` (or the run's `finished_at`) with `closed_day`, `error = 'legacy: completeness unknown'`. None feeds a disappearance.
- Each source row becomes one observation in the run whose window (`started_at` to `finished_at`) contains its `fetched_at`; the row must match exactly one window (zero or several → fail naming table, id, candidate runs); a `(table, id)` in more than one state with a `fetched_at` in the same run must be identical in `(parent, fetched_at, canonical sha256)` or the import aborts. `observed_at` = `fetched_at`, `observed_day` computed, `response_id`/`position` NULL, `parent` = `''` for `categories` (never `categories.parent_id`), the row's own id for `items`, `item_id` for `accounts`/`investments`/`consents`/`identities`, `account_id` for `transactions`/`bills`, `investment_id` for `investment_transactions`. Version bodies are the legacy `raw` parsed and re-serialised canonically, so the first live run does not register a false `changed` on every document.
- Then `--rebuild` sets the checkpoint to run 3.

Verification, failing the import on any mismatch: a manifest of distinct sightings keyed by `(table, id, parent, fetched_at, canonical sha256)` across both states (3,719 on the real pair, the repeated pending row counted once) matched one-to-one against observations; `legacy_*` tables equal the source tables row for row; the projection equals the November state row for row on canonical `raw`, `fetched_at` and every legacy column, `state = 'present'` everywhere, `first_seen_run = 2` for rows in the September state else 3, `last_seen_run = 3` except the repeated pending row at 2; document counts per kind equal the union of ids; `run_coverage` shows runs 1–3 `migrated`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `pluggysync/legacy_import.py`, `pluggysync/cli.py`, `tests/test_legacy_import.py`, `tests/fixtures/legacy_sep.sql`, `tests/fixtures/legacy_nov.sql`
**Reads only:** `pluggysync/rebuild.py`, `pluggysync/ledger.py`, `pluggy_sync.py` (the legacy schema it writes)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On a synthetic fixture pair (built by SQL scripts to the legacy schema, with a run-1-only probe set, a row repeated across states, and an unprobed consent), the import produces the documented runs, scopes (including synthetic consent and movement scopes), observations and legacy tables, and the manifest check passes.
- [ ] A row whose `fetched_at` matches no window, one matching two windows, and a `(table, id)` repeated in one run with a different body each fail with the documented message; a missing `--from-states` fails; a state pair whose `sync_runs` are not a prefix fails.
- [ ] The import never opens `PLUGGY_DB`: with `PLUGGY_DB` pointing at a file that does not exist, the import still succeeds.
- [ ] On a copy of the real frozen pair, the import yields 3,719 observations, runs 1–3 `migrated`, projection parity with the November state as documented, the repeated pending row at `last_seen_run = 2`, `run_coverage` with three migrated runs, and `--check` exits 0 on the result.
- [ ] Done when: `python3 -m unittest` passes and the real-pair import above is recorded in the PR with its counts.

## Tests
Unit over `pluggysync/legacy_import.py` with the synthetic fixture pair (every case above); the real-pair run is a manual acceptance step on a copy, never committed.

## Recovery path
The import writes only the candidate file; deleting it undoes everything. The frozen states and the live database are opened read-only or not at all.
close_reason: Landed via PR #8; the acceptance candidate pluggy.db-candidate was rebuilt from the frozen pair with main's code and --check exits 0 on it (3,719 sightings, 2,019 documents)

title: Add the stack to the homelab repository with its schedule suspended
description:
## What changes for the user
Nothing runs on the server for this project today. After this lands everything is in place and visible in Argo CD, and still does nothing on its own, so the database can be moved over before the first night rather than racing it.

## Outcome
`apps/pluggy-sync/` in the homelab repository, registered in the ApplicationSet and synced by Argo CD, with the CronJob at `suspend: true`, and `check-job.yaml` available for one-off checks.

## Context
The homelab repository is private and Argo CD deploys whatever its `main` holds; a merge is a deploy, and each directory is listed by hand in the ApplicationSet. Its `AGENTS.md` lets the agent merge its own PRs there and holds the rules for this work.

The CronJob ships suspended because the default sync on a directory with no database exits 1 and leaves an empty ledger behind (measured). Argo's `selfHeal` would undo a hand patch of `suspend`, so the state lives in git, and a later PR flips it.

Choices that differ from the other CronJobs there, and why:
- `backoffLimit: 0`: exit 1 is a partial run with its data saved, and exit 3 is usually refused credentials, so a retry repeats 40 API calls and changes nothing. The next night is the retry; the freshness rule tolerates 48 hours.
- `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 259200`: a failed Job keeps `KubeJobFailed` firing until it is deleted, re-notifying every 12 hours. Three days survives a weekend, Loki keeps the logs 7 days, and `runs.note` keeps the reasons forever.
- `activeDeadlineSeconds: 900`: a complete run takes about 15 seconds, the slowest on record 41, and the next night's sweep recovers a killed run.
- `startingDeadlineSeconds: 21600`: a server down at 02:00 catches up until 08:00. A sealed Vault does not block it, since the Secret already exists in the cluster.
- Hardened pod: it holds bank credentials and needs one outbound API and one directory. Non-root, read-only root and dropped capabilities were exercised by the measurement above. `/tmp` is an `emptyDir` because `check.py` uses the default temp directory.
- `PLUGGY_DB` is mandatory: without it the database lands beside the code, inside the container, and disappears with the Job.
- The memory numbers are estimates; `PodOOMKilled` reports a wrong ceiling.

The directory must exist before the merge: the PV uses `DirectoryOrCreate`, which would create it owned by root, and the pod runs as uid 1000.

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: pluggy-sync
  namespace: pluggy-sync
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  timeZone: America/Sao_Paulo
  suspend: true
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 21600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 0
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 900
      ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 259200
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 1000
            runAsGroup: 1000
          containers:
          - name: pluggy-sync
            image: ghcr.io/<owner>/pluggy-sync:0.1.0
            env:
            - name: PLUGGY_DB
              value: /data/pluggy.db
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: pluggy-sync-env
            securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              capabilities:
                drop: [ALL]
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: 50m
                memory: 64Mi
              limits:
                memory: 512Mi
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          volumes:
          - name: data
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: pluggy-sync-data
          - name: tmp
            emptyDir: {}
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `install -d -m 700 /srv/homelab/pluggy-sync` was run as uid 1000 before the merge and logged in the operator's machine log.
- [ ] `apps/pluggy-sync/kustomization.yaml` sets the namespace and lists `secrets.yaml` and `manifests.yaml`, with no domain component since the app has no hostname. `check-job.yaml` is deliberately not listed, so Argo never applies it.
- [ ] `manifests.yaml`: a Namespace (the ApplicationSet sets `CreateNamespace=false`), a static PV `pluggy-sync-data` with `Retain`, `storageClassName: ""`, `claimRef`, `hostPath` on `/srv/homelab/pluggy-sync` with `DirectoryOrCreate`, a PVC with `volumeName`, and the CronJob above. Template: `apps/scrutiny/manifests.yaml:8-38`.
- [ ] `secrets.yaml`: an ExternalSecret `pluggy-sync-env` with store `vault`, kind `ClusterSecretStore`, `refreshInterval: 1h`, `dataFrom.extract.key: homelab/pluggy-sync/pluggy-sync-env`. Template: `apps/python-utils/secrets.yaml:3-18`.
- [ ] `check-job.yaml`: a Job with `generateName: pluggy-check-`, the same pod spec and `args: ["--check"]`, no `envFrom`, and `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600`. Its image line carries the same tag, so the update bot's `apps/**.yaml` coverage moves both.
- [ ] `apps/argocd-config/applicationset.yaml` gains `- path: apps/pluggy-sync`.
- [ ] `scripts/render.sh --clean` passes and the `render` workflow is green. `scripts/probe.sh` reads the same before and after.
- [ ] Argo reports the app Synced; the ExternalSecret reads `SecretSynced`; the Secret's key names, never its values, are the three expected; `kubectl -n pluggy-sync get cronjob` shows `SUSPEND True`; no Job exists.
- [ ] Done when: all of the above hold and the change is in the operator's machine log.

## Tests
- E2E: `scripts/render.sh --clean` renders every directory from the committed tree alone, the same way Argo sees it.
- Manual check: the cluster state in the criterion above, read with `kubectl`.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `apps/pluggy-sync/kustomization.yaml`, `apps/pluggy-sync/manifests.yaml`, `apps/pluggy-sync/secrets.yaml`, `apps/pluggy-sync/check-job.yaml`, `apps/argocd-config/applicationset.yaml`
**Reads only:** `apps/scrutiny/manifests.yaml`, `apps/python-utils/secrets.yaml`, `scripts/render.sh`, `scripts/probe.sh`

All paths are in the homelab repository, a sibling checkout of this one. No file in this repository changes except the tracker. The backup script is not touched: the directory is already inside the nightly restic's roots.

## Recovery path
Revert the PR. Argo prunes the stack; the PV is `Retain`, so the directory stays and holds nothing yet.

title: Make the image package public
description:
## What changes for the user
Until the package is public, the server cannot pull the image and every run would end in `ImagePullBackOff`. After this step the image pulls with no credential on any machine, including a server rebuilt from nothing.

## Outcome
The `pluggy-sync` container package is public, and its code has been checked once against a real ledger.

## Context
This is a hand step. GitHub's documentation says "When you first publish a package, the default visibility is private", and that a package linked to a repository inherits "the access permissions (but not the visibility)" of that repository. Visibility is changed in the package's settings page by the account's owner. The image holds only code already public in this repository, so publishing it exposes nothing new.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The operator sets the package to public under Package settings, Danger Zone, Change visibility.
- [ ] With no credentials, a token from `https://ghcr.io/token?scope=repository:<owner>/pluggy-sync:pull` and a manifest GET for `0.1.0` answer HTTP 200. Nothing is stored on any machine by this check.
- [ ] `--check` in the pulled image, on a private copy of the snapshot in a mode 0700 directory outside the repository, with `--network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp -u 1000:1000 --cap-drop ALL`, prints `check clean`. The copy is deleted afterwards.
- [ ] Done when: both checks passed; the session driving the epic runs them and closes this bead.

## Tests
- Manual check: the anonymous manifest GET is the proof of visibility.
- E2E: `--check` over a real ledger, under the shipped image's real Python and SQLite.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none; one setting on the package.

Nothing in any repository changes.

title: Publish version 0.1.0
description:
## What changes for the user
No released version exists yet, so there is nothing a server could pull. After this lands version 0.1.0 exists in the registry, and that number will always mean the same bytes.

## Outcome
Tag `v0.1.0` on `main`, and image `ghcr.io/<owner>/pluggy-sync:0.1.0` published by the workflow.

## Context
The image workflow publishes on a `v*` tag and refuses to overwrite an existing image tag. GitHub makes a package private on its first publish, whatever the repository's visibility, so right after this bead the image exists and can only be pulled with credentials. A separate bead assigned to the operator makes it public.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `v0.1.0` points at a `main` commit that contains the image workflow, and it is pushed.
- [ ] The tag's workflow run concludes `success`; its log shows the test stage ran and the smoke test passed.
- [ ] `gh api /users/<owner>/packages/container/pluggy-sync/versions` lists tag `0.1.0`.
- [ ] Re-running the tag's workflow fails at the step refusing an existing tag; the run id goes in the close reason.
- [ ] Done when: the package exists at `0.1.0` and the operator has been told the visibility step is theirs.

## Tests
- E2E: the workflow's own test stage and smoke test, on the tagged commit.
- Manual check: the re-run above proves the refusal against the real registry, which no PR run can do.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none in the tree; one git tag, one registry package.

The tag is a release, not a file change, and the image is the only thing it publishes.

## Recovery path
A broken release is replaced by the next version, never overwritten. A package version can be deleted from the package's settings page, but no deployment refers to this one yet.

Run 42530392098: attempt 1 denied by the registry at the manifest push after every layer uploaded, cause not established; attempt 2 ran 293 tests, passed the smoke test and pushed 0.1.0 at digest sha256:968f6825294d. Attempt 3 failed at the refusal step with: tag 0.1.0 already exists, refusing. The package listing API needs a read:packages scope the local token lacks; the refusal and the push digest stand in for it until the anonymous pull in the next bead.

title: Turn the schedule on and stop the desktop collecting
description:
## What changes for the user
Collecting still takes someone remembering to run a command, and running it on the desktop now would start a second, diverging history. After this lands collection happens by itself every night, a stray run on the desktop refuses instead of forking the data, and the way to read the ledger is one copy command.

## Outcome
The CronJob's `suspend` is `false` in git, the desktop's `pluggy.db` is renamed aside, and the on-demand read path is proved.

## Context
The default sync refuses a database with no cutover row (the marker that a ledger was promoted to live): with the file renamed, a run on the desktop creates an empty ledger and exits 1 (measured on an empty directory). With the credentials absent it exits 2 and writes nothing. Either way it cannot quietly start a second history, so the credentials do not need removing.

The read path is a copy of the snapshot rather than a query against the live file: the snapshot is replaced by atomic rename, so a copy can never be torn, and working on a copy cannot disturb the ledger. It costs freshness of up to one day, which the data has anyway. A timer or a mount was rejected as building for a need that has not appeared.

The next two beads need time to pass, and a dependency cannot express that: one needs a scheduled night to have happened, and the other needs a week of them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A PR in the homelab repository sets `suspend: false` in `apps/pluggy-sync/manifests.yaml`, merged before 01:30 local time. `kubectl -n pluggy-sync get cronjob` shows `SUSPEND False`.
- [ ] On the desktop, `pluggy.db` is renamed to `pluggy.db-desktop-final-<YYYY-MM-DD>`, kept and not deleted. The pattern `pluggy.db-*` already ignores it in git.
- [ ] `scp -p` of `/srv/homelab/pluggy-sync/pluggy-snapshot.db` into the desktop checkout succeeds, the copy is mode 0600, and one tested query from the README runs against it with `sqlite3`.
- [ ] `br defer pluggy-1k1 --until` the morning after the merge, and `br defer pluggy-992 --until` seven days after it.
- [ ] Done when: the above hold and the change is in the operator's machine log.

## Tests
- E2E: the `scp` and README query above are the read path, exercised once for real.
- Manual check: `kubectl` shows the schedule live; the next bead proves it fired.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `apps/pluggy-sync/manifests.yaml` in the homelab repository; one file renamed in the desktop checkout.

Nothing in this repository's code changes.

## Recovery path
Revert the PR to suspend the schedule. Rename the desktop file back only if the server is being abandoned, and first copy the server's ledger over it: the server's history is the newer one.

title: Make repair modes and the code version work without git
description:
## What changes for the user
Inside a container there is no git. Today the commands for repairing a database stop with a Python traceback there, on exactly the day they are needed, and every run records its code version as "unknown", so nobody can later tell which code wrote which run. After this lands the repair commands behave the same with or without git, and each run records the version the image was built from.

## Outcome
`code_version` honours a `PLUGGY_CODE_VERSION` environment variable, and `check_candidate_path` treats a missing `git` binary as "not inside a repository".

## Context
Measured by running the suite in `python:3-alpine` (Python 3.14.7, Alpine 3.24.1, SQLite 3.53.2, no git): 288 tests, 257 pass, 31 errors, no assertion failures. 28 of the errors are `FileNotFoundError: 'git'`, raised by `check_candidate_path` (`pluggysync/cli.py:61-84`), which calls `git rev-parse` and `git check-ignore` with no guard. It runs behind `--candidate`, `--promote` and `--reparse`. `--reparse` rebuilds a corrected copy of the history from the raw response archive, so it is the tool that must work on a bad day.

`code_version` (`pluggysync/run.py:64-75`) already guards and returns `unknown`, which is safe and useless: `runs.code_version` is the only record of what wrote a run, and `pluggysync/promote.py` already ignores runs whose version is `unknown` when it looks for a live run to accept.

The refusal in `check_candidate_path` exists to keep a database out of version control. Where git is absent there is no version control to protect, so returning the path is correct. Only the absence of the binary changes behaviour: a directory that git reports as a repository, and a path git does not ignore there, are still refused.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With `PLUGGY_CODE_VERSION=v0.0.0-abc` set, `code_version` returns `v0.0.0-abc` without starting a subprocess.
- [ ] With the variable empty or unset, `code_version` behaves exactly as today: `git describe` output, or `unknown` when git fails or is absent.

title: Run the real-data acceptance on the candidate ledger
description:
## What changes for the user
Everything built so far has been proven on synthetic data. Once this lands, the new database has been run once against the real bank connections on top of the imported history, and every question the project promised (balance as of a day, caixinha yield between two days, a transaction's edit history, the clean list) has been answered on real data with each value traced to the response it came from.

## Outcome
A candidate database built from the two frozen states has one real API run on it, `--check` is clean, every README example query has been executed on it with its result recorded, and the archive's real size per run is known.

## Context
The candidate is produced by `--candidate <path> --from-states pluggy.db-2026-09-12-state pluggy.db-2026-11-07-state`, then `--candidate <path>` (no `--from-states`) runs one live ledger sync against the real API with the three `PLUGGY_*` variables. Runs are manual today (no scheduler exists until the deployment plan), so this run does not overlap any other API use. The candidate path must be outside the repository or git-ignored; it holds personal data and is `0600`.

What the evidence should show, and what is **not** fixed in advance:
- Outcome `complete`, every expected scope `complete` or `unavailable`, no ambiguity.
- The pending card purchase captured on 2026-09-12 and absent on 2026-11-07: `removed` **if** its account's walk `min_date` on the acceptance day is on or before the purchase date (today that walk returns from a year earlier); otherwise it stays `present`, uncovered, and appears in the unresolved list. Assert whichever the evidence supports, never a fixed answer.
- `reserved_balance_history` for the run has as many rows as reserves in that run's archived account responses (a reserve opened or closed since the frozen data legitimately changes the count).
- `run_coverage` shows runs 1–3 `migrated` and run 4 `complete`.
- Every file created is `0600`: database, lock, journal, temporary.
- `responses.raw_bytes` and `length(body_zlib)` summed for the run give the real archive size (the plan's estimate, ~2.7 MB raw and ~10% after zlib, is unverified).
- Every README example query executed: balance as of 2026-09-12 and 2026-11-07 with coverage status; reserve balances as of each of the three days; caixinha yield between 2026-09-12 and 2026-11-07 and between 2026-11-07 and the run day (expected numeric for reserves whose transfers all match; NULL with reason for transfers naming renamed or deleted reserves and for any uncovered window); CDB history; the replaced pending transaction's history; the clean list and the unresolved list for its account.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `README.md` (the measured archive size and the acceptance record), `tests/test_acceptance_queries.py` (the README queries as tests over the synthetic fixture, so they stay runnable)
**Reads only:** everything else; no code change is expected. A code defect found here is fixed in its own bead's module and lands as a fix referencing this bead.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The candidate exists, built from the frozen pair, and `--check` exits 0 before the live run.
- [ ] One live run against the API closes `complete`; `--check` exits 0 afterwards; `run_coverage` shows four runs as described.
- [ ] The replaced pending row is in the state the evidence supports, with the walk's `min_date` recorded beside the assertion.
- [ ] `reserved_balance_history` row count for run 4 equals the reserve count in the archived account responses of run 4.
- [ ] Every README example query runs on the candidate and its output (or unknown reason) is recorded in the PR, each value traced to `observation_id`s.
- [ ] Archive bytes for run 4 (raw and compressed) are recorded in the README.
- [ ] `ls -l` of every file the run created shows `0600`.
- [ ] Done when: the PR carries the recorded outputs and the README change, and the candidate file is kept for the promotion bead.

## Tests
E2e, manual, against the real API on the candidate (recorded, not committed). Unit: the README queries encoded as tests over the synthetic fixture so a later change that breaks a query is caught.

## Recovery path
The candidate is a separate file; deleting it undoes the run. The live database is not opened.

title: Project the ledger into current-state tables, history views, rebuild and candidate mode
description:
## What changes for the user
Today the database can answer "what is my balance now" and nothing about yesterday: the balance of each reserve sub-account (a Mercado Pago caixinha), the limit of each card and the value of each CDB are overwritten every run. Once this lands, every balance as of any past day, the full edit history of any transaction, a clean transaction list that does not count a pending purchase twice, and the yield of each caixinha between two days are SQL queries documented in the README, and the ledger can be run against a candidate copy of the database without touching the live one.

## Outcome
The current-state tables gain history columns and are rebuildable from the ledger; `--rebuild` regenerates them atomically; `projection_state` checkpoints the last projected run and recovery projects what a crash left behind; the views `run_coverage`, `scope_coverage`, `account_balance_history`, `reserved_balance_history`, `investment_history`, `transaction_versions`, `pending_posted_candidates` exist; `--candidate <path>` runs the ledger sync against a dedicated copy; the README is revised with every example query and the false "verbatim" claim removed.

## Context
Vocabulary: the ledger records every HTTP attempt (`responses`), every sighting of a document version (`observations`, with `observed_day` stored at ingest), per-run walks (`scopes`, with `infer_absence` saying whether a complete walk may infer absence and `min_date` the earliest business date it returned), and derived `events` and `ambiguities`. Projections are the nine current-state tables that exist today (`items`, `accounts`, `transactions`, `bills`, `investments`, `investment_transactions`, `consents`, `identities`, `categories`), kept with their names, extracted columns and indexes so existing queries keep working.

Projection rows: `raw` = canonical body of the latest sighting; `fetched_at` = latest sighting's `observed_at`; parent columns (`transactions.account_id`, `bills.account_id`, `investment_transactions.investment_id`, `item_id` columns) come from `observations.parent`, never the body (bills and investment transactions carry no parent in their JSON); `items` has no parent column; `categories.parent_id` is the body's `parentId` (the category tree). New columns: `first_seen_run NOT NULL` (never overwritten), `last_seen_run NOT NULL`, `state IN ('present','removed','parent_gone') NOT NULL`, `ambiguous_run`. An ambiguous document's display row is the deterministic sighting (lowest `parent`, lowest `sha256`, highest `id`).

**Checkpoint and recovery**: `projection_state(id = 1, projected_run, code_version)`; an absent row means 0. Recovery projects every terminal run with `id > projected_run` in id order (events, projections, per-run self-check, checkpoint), stopping non-zero before advancing over a run whose self-check fails. `--rebuild` replays every run in id order regardless of outcome and must equal the incremental result, checkpoint included.

**`--rebuild`** inside one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`: build `new_*` projection tables, `new_events`, `new_ambiguities` with primary keys only (secondary index names are schema-global), validate, drop the views, drop the old tables, rename `new_*` into place, create `transactions_by_date`, `transactions_by_account`, `events_by_document`, recreate the views, write the checkpoint (delete the row if `runs` is empty), commit. `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME` validates every view, so this order is the one that works (reproduced on SQLite 3.53.4); a failure at any point rolls back.

**Clean list**: a row is clean when `present`, `ambiguous_run IS NULL`, covered (`scope_coverage.last_absence_safe_run = projected_run` and, for dated kinds, business date `>= last_min_date`), and, for a `PENDING` transaction, not matched in `pending_posted_candidates`. Rows present but not covered are "last observed, not covered". A pending transaction not covered, or matched in candidates, is **unresolved** and never clean. `pending_posted_candidates(account_id, pending_id, pending_date, pending_observed_at, pending_covered, posted_id, posted_date, posted_observed_at, amount, currency, description)` pairs a `PENDING` and a `POSTED` row on one account, both present and unambiguous, the posted covered, same `currency`, `amount`, `description` and UTC calendar date `substr(date, 1, 10)` (59 of the 62 pending-to-posted transitions in the frozen data moved the time of day by 3 h).

**As-of semantics**: historical queries use only rows with `observed_day`/`closed_day` up to D, never today's `state` or coverage. Coverage at D: `no_run` when no run has `D BETWEEN started_day AND COALESCE(finished_day, started_day)`; `covered` when the `(kind, parent)` had a scope with `closed_day = D` and `infer_absence = 1` (and date `>= min_date`); else `not covered`.

**Views** (ids are `documents.provider_id`; `day` = `observed_day`; several sightings in one local day → latest run, then unambiguous sighting with highest `id`, or the display sighting if ambiguous):
- `run_coverage(run_id, started_at, started_day, finished_at, finished_day, outcome, expected, complete, unavailable, incomplete, skipped, pending, ambiguous_documents)`: outcome columns count `expected = 1` scopes and partition `expected`; `pending > 0` on a terminal run is an alarm; no row for a day without a run (README queries generate the calendar and show `no_run`).
- `account_balance_history(run_id, day, observed_at, provider_updated_at, account_id, observation_id, name, type, currency, balance, closing_balance, automatically_invested_balance, credit_limit, available_credit_limit)`.
- `reserved_balance_history(run_id, day, observed_at, provider_updated_at, account_id, observation_id, position, reserve_id, stable_identity, reserve_name, currency, amount, indexer, indexer_ratio, cdi_percentage, amount_status)` over `json_each(body, '$.bankData.reservedBalances')` guarded by `json_type(...) = 'array'` (some accounts carry `null`, which `json_each` would turn into one all-NULL row); `position` is the array index; `reserve_id` = `identification`, `stable_identity = 1` only when non-empty and unique within the observation; `amount`, `currency`, `indexer`, `indexer_ratio` (`availableAmounts[0].remuneration.postFixedIndexerPercentage`, a ratio like `1.199983`) and `cdi_percentage` (`ratio * 100` only when `indexer = 'CDI'`) come from the single `availableAmounts` element when exactly one exists (`amount_status = 'ok'`), else all NULL with the reason. A reserve as of D is read by selecting the latest account observation by D from `account_balance_history` first and `LEFT JOIN`ing this view on `observation_id`, so an emptied array is not skipped and nothing is carried forward.
- `investment_history(run_id, day, observed_at, provider_updated_at, provider_date, investment_id, name, currency, amount_original, amount_gross, taxes, taxes2, amount_net, rate, rate_type, due_date, status)`; `taxes` reads as provisioned income tax and `taxes2` as provisioned IOF (non-zero only on a CDB bought inside the 30-day IOF window), inferred from values, stated as such in the README.
- `transaction_versions(document_id, provider_id, account_id, run_id, day, observed_at, provider_updated_at, sha256, status, date, amount, currency, description, category, bill_post_date, events, ambiguous)`: `kind = 'transactions'`, over observations ordered by `(run_id, id)`; a row for every sighting whose `(sha256, parent, ambiguous)` differs from the previous or whose `(run_id, document_id)` has an `events` row; `events` is the comma-joined labels in `seq` order, NULL otherwise.

**Money**: JSON numbers arrive as floats. README arithmetic validates (finite, `abs < 1e12`, two-decimal currency, at most two decimals after rounding to 1e-9), converts with `CAST(round(x * 100) AS INTEGER)`, returns unknown for a failing input; `amountOriginal` has sub-cent digits after partial withdrawals and is never summed.

**Caixinha yield** (README query, two local days D1 < D2): `prev`/`curr` are the latest unambiguous account observations by D1/D2 whose `reservedBalances` is an array (the account walk's outcome is irrelevant: the array is self-contained, so migrated runs qualify); `provider_updated_at` must parse with `prev < curr`. Result = union of stable reserve ids in `prev` and `curr`, plus unjoined rows for unstable entries (reason `unstable`); only in `curr` → starts at 0; only in `prev` → NULL yield, reason `closed or missing at D2`. Transfers: latest unambiguous version known by D2 of `TRANSFERENCIA_SALDO_RESERVADO` transactions on the account, `present` as of D2, `date > prev.provider_updated_at AND date <= curr.provider_updated_at` (bounded by the provider timestamp, not the collection day: on 2026-09-12 five transfers at 17:34–17:36 UTC were already in the 18:17 UTC snapshot), each used only if `POSTED`, covered by an absence-safe walk, in no candidate pair, and with prefix agreeing with sign (`'Dinheiro reservado '` with `amount < 0`, `'Dinheiro retirado '` with `amount > 0`); matched by description to a name that identifies exactly one stable reserve id in every unambiguous account observation from `prev` through `curr` (about a quarter of the transfers in the frozen data name reserves renamed or deleted since; those yield unknown). `yield_cents = (curr - prev) + SUM(tx)`. NULL with reason (`unstable`, `name changed`, `name reused`, `unmatched transfer`, `transfer removed`, `transfer pending`, `transfer unresolved`, `transfer sign`, `coverage gap`, `currency`, `amount`) when any condition fails, when the account's transactions scope at `curr`'s run was not absence-safe with `min_instant <= prev.provider_updated_at`, or when a cutoff has no qualifying observation.

**`--candidate <path>`** creates or verifies a dedicated candidate database and runs the ledger sync against it; refuses the configured live database, any path with the same inode, and any path inside the repository that `git check-ignore` does not report as ignored. (Historical import and promotion are later beads.) The default sync stays the legacy path until cutover.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** `pluggysync/projections.py`, `pluggysync/views.py`, `pluggysync/rebuild.py`, `pluggysync/cli.py`, `pluggy_sync.py` (dispatch to `cli.py`), `README.md`, `tests/test_projections.py`, `tests/test_views.py`, `tests/test_rebuild.py`, `tests/test_cli_candidate.py`
**Reads only:** `pluggysync/events.py`, `pluggysync/run.py`, `pluggysync/ledger.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a multi-run fixture, every projection table equals the result of `--rebuild` row for row (including `first_seen_run`, `last_seen_run`, `state`, `ambiguous_run`) and `projection_state.projected_run` equals the last run; the same after a crash injected after a scope commit and one during run close, with recovery projecting the interrupted run first.
- [ ] `--rebuild` interrupted (injected failure) at each of: after building `new_*`, after dropping views, after dropping old tables, after renaming, leaves the previous tables, indexes and views usable and `--rebuild` succeeds on retry; no `new_*` or temporary index remains after success; `--rebuild` on an empty `runs` leaves no `projection_state` row.
- [ ] `reserved_balance_history` on the frozen-shape fixture returns one row per reserve entry; on accounts with `reservedBalances` null, absent, `[]`, an unnamed entry, a duplicate `identification`, zero and two `availableAmounts` elements, and a non-CDI indexer returns the documented values; the as-of query for an account whose latest observation has `[]` returns no reserve.
- [ ] `transaction_versions` shows two rows for a transaction removed then reappeared with the same body, two rows for a move with an identical body, two rows for two different bodies in one run, and one row for 365 identical daily sightings.
- [ ] `pending_posted_candidates` pairs the replaced-pending fixture (pending uncovered, posted covered, dates differing by 3 h on the same UTC day) and the clean list contains neither member; a pending row dated before the latest walk's `min_date` is unresolved and not clean.
- [ ] Coverage after a `failed` run in which account A's walk completed and B's did not: A's documents clean, B's "last observed, not covered"; an item id removed from configuration leaves its documents present, uncovered, not clean, with no removal event.
- [ ] The yield query on a fixture reproducing 2026-09-12 (five transfers before the snapshot's `updatedAt`) returns the correct yield once, not double-counted; a reserve opened between cutoffs starts at 0; one closed between them returns NULL with `closed or missing at D2`; a rename, a reuse visible only in an intermediate observation, two reserves sharing a name, an unstable entry, a transfer removed before D2, one pending, one in a candidate pair, one with a wrong sign, a walk not reaching back to `prev.provider_updated_at`, and a transfer edited after D2 (answer for D2 unchanged) each return the documented reason; `prev` taken from a migrated run is accepted.
- [ ] `--candidate` pointed at the live `PLUGGY_DB`, at a relative alias of it, and at an un-ignored path inside the repository exits non-zero without writing; pointed at an ignored path creates a `0600` candidate and runs the ledger sync against it.
- [ ] The README documents every view and every example query (balance as of a day with coverage, reserve as of a day, caixinha yield, CDB history, a transaction's history, the clean list, the unresolved list), the archive, locks, backups and modes, and no longer says `raw` is verbatim.
- [ ] Done when: `python3 -m unittest` passes with every case above and the README changes are in the same PR.

## Tests
Unit over `pluggysync/projections.py`, `views.py`, `rebuild.py` and `cli.py` on temporary databases with hand-built ledger fixtures (no HTTP): every case above; a recorded-expected-output test per view on a fixed fixture; the rebuild-equals-incremental assertion over a five-run fixture with injected crashes.

## Recovery path
`--rebuild` is itself the recovery for a damaged projection; the ledger tables are not written by this bead. The legacy database is untouched.

title: Store the Pluggy credentials in Vault
description:
## What changes for the user
The credentials exist only in a shell file on one desktop, and the server cannot read them. After this step the cluster gets them from Vault the same way every other stack does, and nothing about them is in a repository.

## Outcome
`secret/homelab/pluggy-sync/pluggy-sync-env` holds `PLUGGY_CLIENT_ID`, `PLUGGY_CLIENT_SECRET` and `PLUGGY_ITEM_IDS`.

## Context
This is a hand step: it needs the Vault operator token, which only the operator holds. The server has no `vault` binary; the CLI runs inside the pod `vault-0` in namespace `vault`. External Secrets reads any path under `secret/homelab/`, so no policy change is needed. The stored value is verbatim, so no quotes are written. The shell file that holds the values does not export them, so `set -a` goes around sourcing it.

The session driving the epic prepares the exact command and hands it over. The values reach Vault through stdin as JSON (`vault kv put <path> -`), never as arguments: an argument lands in shell history and in `ps`, and an agent that typed it would have put a bank credential in its transcript. No agent reads these values.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The operator runs the prepared command.
- [ ] `vault kv get -format=json` piped through a key-names-only filter lists exactly the three keys. Values are not printed.
- [ ] The operator's machine log carries an entry naming the path, not the values.
- [ ] Done when: the three key names are confirmed.

## Tests
- Manual check: the key listing above. The end-to-end proof that the values are right is the first real run, in a later bead.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none in any repository; one path in Vault.

Other Vault paths and policies are not touched.

## Recovery path
`vault kv metadata delete secret/homelab/pluggy-sync/pluggy-sync-env`. A wrong value is corrected by writing the path again, then letting External Secrets resync.
close_reason: Vault path written by the operator at version 1; key listing shows exactly PLUGGY_CLIENT_ID, PLUGGY_CLIENT_SECRET, PLUGGY_ITEM_IDS. Values never printed. Logged in the machine log.

title: Check the restored ledger and clean up
description:
## What changes for the user
Coming back from off-site is only half the test: the file also has to be whole and recent. After this lands that is known, and restoring is a procedure that has been done rather than one that is written down.

## Outcome
The restored ledger checks clean in the real image and holds the most recent run that the backup could have seen.

## Context
`check-job.yaml` is the one-off Job that runs `--check` with the deployment's pod spec. Pointing it at the restored file only changes `PLUGGY_DB`. `max(runs.id)` is what separates a recent backup from an old one that happens to be intact, since `--check` alone would pass on a file weeks old. The directory must go afterwards, or the next backup keeps a second copy of the data.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `check-job.yaml` with `PLUGGY_DB=/data/restore-test/pluggy.db` logs `check clean`.
- [ ] `max(runs.id)` in the restored file equals the id of the last run finished before that backup started.
- [ ] `/srv/homelab/pluggy-sync/restore-test/` is removed.
- [ ] Done when: the above hold; the result goes in the private acceptance record, the counts only.

## Tests
- E2E: `--check` over the restored bytes, in the shipped image, on the real node.

## Blast radius
**Edits:** none in any repository; the temporary directory is removed.
**Reads only:** `apps/pluggy-sync/check-job.yaml`

The live ledger is not touched.
